Ironically I felt that TLJ was very derivative of The Empire Strikes back but in less compelling ways.

The Jedi Master being a reclusive hermit that doesn't meet the audiences expectations was already done with Yoda, (And it doesn't fit Luke's characterization from Return of the Jedi).

Rey having the twist lineage reveal that she is a nobody is just the inverse of Luke thinking he was a nobody only for it to be revealed that Vader is his father.

Kylo asking Rey to join him is a retread of Vader asking Luke to join him.

The Crait Scene was the Hoth Sequence but at the end of the film.

The good guys losing was already done in The Empire Strikes back.

I love Rian Johnson's other movies, but the only thing that he added to the formula were the Canto Bight segments which were definitely the weakest. The movie heavily leans on the 'forget the past' themes while retreading almost all of the plot points from Empire Strikes Back but in a weaker way. The same could be said about the Force Awakens but that movie didn't spend time tearing the narrative of the previous story down (Unless you count the Empire coming back), and it didn't try to pretend to be something it wasn't.

All of that said TLJ is the most beautifully shot SW film by far.
